title: Bounded constructible complexes
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be a closed symmetric monoidal Grothendieck abelian category whose tensor product is additive, let $X$ be a scheme with small pro-etale site $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and give $\mathcal S=\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal A)$ the sheaf tensor product of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Let $\mathcal R$ be a commutative ring object of $\mathcal S$ [sk-def-sfb-ring-object], and write $\Mod_{\mathcal R}=\Mod_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal S)$ for its category of left module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Use the ordinary unbounded derived category $D(\Mod_{\mathcal R})$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with the unbounded convention of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories].

In this definition, constructibility of an $\mathcal R$-module $M$ means precisely the general ring-object predicate [def-sfb-constructible-module]: there is a finite stratification by immersions $g_a:X_a\to X$ such that $\operatorname{mapMod}(g_a^*)(M)$ is locally finitely presented over $g_a^*\mathcal R$ on each stratum. This specifies the predicate for arbitrary $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal R$.

A complex $K\in D(\Mod_{\mathcal R})$ is *bounded constructible* if it is bounded for the canonical t-structure, meaning that there exist integers $a\leq b$ such that $H^n(K)=0$ whenever $n<a$ or $b<n$, and every cohomology module object $H^n(K)$, $n\in\mathbf Z$, is constructible in the specified sense. The *bounded constructible derived category* $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal R)$ is the full subcategory of $D(\Mod_{\mathcal R})$ on these objects; its morphisms are exactly the ambient derived-category morphisms. No derived completeness condition is imposed.
